name: English

pronunciation.note: Optional approximate English sound guide. Read in your own natural voice and accent.

samplePronunciation.latin: This iz my voys, RED-ee tuh tel thuh nekst STOR-ee.
samplePronunciation.note: Approximate English sounds; keep your own comfortable accent.

name: Arabic
prompt: أسجّل صوتي لصناعة تعليق واضح وطبيعي. أتحدث بهدوء وبسرعتي المعتادة، مع وقفة قصيرة بين الأفكار.

pronunciation.note: Approximate Standard Arabic transliteration. ā/ī/ū are long vowels; ʿ and ḥ need the audio example. Spoken case endings may vary.

samplePronunciation.latin: Hādhā ṣawtī, jāhizun li-riwāyati al-qiṣṣati al-qādimah.
samplePronunciation.note: Approximate Standard Arabic transliteration. ā/ī are long vowels; listen for dh, ṣ and q. Spoken case endings may vary.

name: Spanish

pronunciation.note: Approximate Spanish sounds, using Latin American s in narración. Listen for your example’s regional pronunciation; rr is rolled.

samplePronunciation.note: Approximate Spanish sounds. Regional accents vary; keep the vowels short and clear.

name: Mandarin Chinese

pronunciation.note: Mandarin pinyin: tone marks are essential. Pinyin letters such as q, x and zh are not pronounced as English letters.

pronunciation.note: Approximate Japanese romanization. ē is a long vowel; keep syllables even and listen for pitch and light or unvoiced vowels.

name: Korean
